sample_unit: ICU consultant annotators (each yielding a model)
models_evaluated: 11 supervised classifiers trained on individual ICU consultant annotations

links.outcome: Agreement between models trained on different experts' labels on external validation
links.effect: Internal Fleiss' κ = 0.383 (fair); external pairwise average Cohen's κ = 0.255 (minimal); discharge κ = 0.174 vs mortality κ = 0.267; majority vote consensus consistently suboptimal.
links.quote: Further, broad external validation (on both static and time series datasets) of these 11 classifiers was carried out on a HiRID external dataset, where the models' classifications were found to have low pairwise agreements (average Cohen's κ = 0.255 i.e., minimal agreement).

unlisted_practices: Assessing annotation learnability and using only learnable annotated datasets to determine consensus labels

screen.reason: Evaluates how inconsistencies in clinical expert annotation affect model training and compares consensus practices (such as majority vote vs learnability filtering) to obtain reliable clinical predictive models.
